Research on the collective motion of rotating distorted halo nuclei will advance significantly with upcoming experiments at facilities like FRIB and HIAF. These studies focus on spinning nuclei with unusual surface structures, such as the $^{11}$Be and $^{19}$C halos. A key concept in these experiments is "shape uncoupling," which describes the independent rotation of the core and halo components. As a result, shape uncoupling leads to enhanced collective motion when the nuclei are spinning. To investigate this phenomenon, we applied the antisymmetrized local density approximation to calculate the collective motion of spinning $^{11}$Be and $^{19}$C nuclei. Our findings show that shape uncoupling effects are prominent at low spin rates but diminish as the nuclei spin faster. Consequently, these effects can lead to increased frequency shifts in certain nuclear motions. The magnitude of these shifts can be influenced by the location of a nucleon at the edge of the halo. Our research also highlights the need for more accurate theoretical models to better understand these nuclei.

We've developed an advanced video super-resolution model, which we've named BasicVSR++, by expanding upon our previously released BasicVSR. The two key innovations in BasicVSR++ are the incorporation of cross-frame attention and a new feature alignment strategy. The added attention mechanism facilitates a more effective exchange of information between neighboring frames, while the feature alignment strategy ensures that enhanced edge features are accurately matched between neighboring frames. Furthermore, we've expanded the model's capacity by integrating deformable convolution. The combination of these improvements has significantly boosted BasicVSR++'s video enhancement performance. Theoretical analysis and the concept of inter-frame attention exchange can be found in the appendix. The results from the benchmarks and the end-to-end training strategy for BasicVSR++ have also been detailed. The experiments reveal that BasicVSR++ has outperformed BasicVSR and the current video super-resolution models on the standard test datasets.

A precision measurement of the vector boson scattering (VBS) cross-section at a muon collider is proposed, leveraging a $\sqrt{s}=10$ TeV collision and focusing on the $W^+W^+\ell^-\ell^-$ final state. A sophisticated vector boson tagging approach is employed, utilizing kinematic information from the undetected neutrinos to enhance the efficiency of identifying the vector bosons. This method significantly enhances the signal sample, increasing the visible phase space coverage by a factor of 10 compared to existing techniques. As a result, we can measure the total VBS cross-section with an impressive 10% precision, surpassing the 200 GeV CMS capabilities at a $\mu\mu$ collider. A detailed analysis of the relevant background sources and the associated uncertainties is also presented.

Achieving a balance between diversity and cohesion in a model that's
utilized for various purposes in model-based reinforcement learning has been
shown to be a significant challenge. A key advantage of a diverse model is its
ability to be applied to multiple tasks, while a cohesive model yields optimal
results in any given task. Our research suggests that a decentralized structure
for reinforcement learning models can address this challenge effectively. Our
proposed approach of creating modular reinforcement learning models with
sub-modules that model distinct aspects of the environment and integrate them
through a learning mechanism that minimizes interference among the sub-modules
proves to be a versatile framework. Our results demonstrate that our model can
identify structural similarities in the environment, acquire optimal policies
for a variety of tasks efficiently, and even adapt dynamically to environments
with diverse destruction and optimal policies. Our findings suggest that modular
reinforcement learning models may be the path to robust artificial intelligence
systems capable of operating in a wide range of real-world environments.

The paper provides a method to derive a specific approximation scheme, which can be used to obtain similar approximation methods for a variety of equations, including the p-Laplace equation, the p-Sobolev equation, and the Vazquez equation. These approximation methods are developed in the context of a complete, non-compact metric measure space that has a bounded, compact domain.

We synthesize key elements of the Godel-Carnap-Tarski-Godel program,
which sought to surpass classical semanticism via formalization and model
theory, achieving a comprehensive theory of types. This theory encompassed
independent insights into the limitations of logical systems, drawing on
Godel's work on provability and decidability. Our work provides a detailed
explanation of Godel's innovative approach to proving the Bar Theorem.

In Clifford analysis, an integral representation analogous to Cauchy's formula exists. This representation enables an expression for a Dirac operator's eigenfunctions at any point within a closed domain as an integral over the boundary surface. Furthermore, a integral representation exists for coefficients in a series expansion of these eigenfunctions. This series involves a series of nested spheres and resembles a Foster series for power series coefficients. Consequently, values of a Dirac operator's eigenfunctions at any set of nested spheres can be determined through a series of such nested spheres.

When surveying a large population, selecting a geographically balanced sample is crucial for accurate results. This task becomes increasingly complex when dealing with large populations spread across multiple regions. Our solution is a novel algorithm called Sequential Geographically Balanced Sampling (SeqGABS), which efficiently selects a balanced sample from various regions. SeqGABS can run on several processors simultaneously and has been shown to produce geographically balanced outcomes. The algorithm's sequential design allows for gradual population data input, making it suitable for real-world applications.

Adjusting eye-in-hand cameras is essential to ensure accurate visual feedback in robotic systems. Using onboard sensors, we can calibrate these cameras to achieve precise image measurements. However, existing methods rely on detecting known objects within the scene. We propose an alternative approach that uses just one image to adjust the camera. This method leverages a neural network to identify natural image patterns that remain consistent across multiple views. We conducted experiments using simulated scenes and real cameras, and our method successfully calibrated the eye-in-hand camera with high accuracy.

The goal of restoring a target image is to revert a degraded version back to its original state. This task is a common application in solving inverse problems. The success of this process is significantly influenced by the prior chosen to guide the restoration. Traditional methods often rely on explicit, hand-crafted priors, which can be limited in capturing complex relationships between target pixels. The development of conditional generative adversarial networks has shown great potential in defining implicit priors for conditional tasks. Our proposed model, R$^2$-CFGAN, builds on this by incorporating guided conditional fusion into the network architecture, enabling more controlled and consistent predictions. The results of our approach on various super-resolution datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of R$^2$-CFGAN in achieving high-quality restorations.

This article investigates why certain dynamical systems of higher order cannot exhibit specific behaviors by analyzing how their trajectories evolve over time within various subspaces. We apply this investigation to a specific system previously studied in the context of financial modeling, which involved three variables representing asset price, market demand, and supply, and found that its dynamics cannot be effectively understood through its behavior on particular two-dimensional subspaces.

Next-generation wireless networks, utilizing Terahertz (THz) frequency bands, have the potential to provide extremely high data transfer rates.  However, due to rapid THz signal degradation, directional beam training is necessary to overcome this limitation.  In THz multi-hop links, the number of possible combinations of transmit and receive beams at each node escalates exponentially with the addition of each node, significantly hindering efficiency.  This paper proposes a novel, end-to-end link approach, reducing the number of nodes requiring beamforming by one, and presents a reinforcement learning-based method for rapid beam training that learns the optimal local configuration at each node and facilitates the creation of a stable, high-capacity THz link.  Simulation results demonstrate that this approach can achieve a high link throughput with a link length of up to 10 meters, using a method that is both computationally efficient and easy to implement.

The interstellar medium's impact on radio signals from bright pulsars can be used to study the galaxy's radio-scintillation pattern and provide insights into the interstellar medium on small scales. This study focuses on the anomalous pulsar B1133+16, which exhibits unusual features in its interstellar-scintillation pattern that are not commonly seen in other pulsars. By analyzing the unusual characteristics of its scintillation pattern, a scale of about 0.1 parsecs is probed, revealing a complex pattern of turbulence in the galaxy's interstellar medium. A detailed analysis of the power spectrum of its scintillation pattern is conducted, which reveals a distinct break in its form at a specific frequency of about 0.1 Hz. This frequency is not consistent with predictions from Kolmogorov turbulence, which instead suggests a range of competing-turbulence models. The authors suggest that a two-component fit to the data is necessary to fully capture the complexity of the scintillation pattern, which in turn provides a more accurate estimate of the scale of the turbulence. This study highlights the importance of radio-scintillation studies in understanding the interstellar medium and emphasizes the need for further research using pulsars as natural radio telescopes.

This paper introduces the Quasi-Periodic WaveNet, a novel generative model for audio signal reconstruction, which addresses the limitations of existing models in capturing audio's quasi-periodic characteristics. Unlike previous models, Quasi-Periodic WaveNet incorporates a Quasi-Periodic Convolution Neural Network that utilizes a dual dual-dilated convolution structure to efficiently extract local and global audio features. This structure is optimized for both spatial and temporal dimensionality reduction, and is further enhanced by a learnable kernel size control mechanism. Furthermore, the model's inference speed is significantly improved through the use of parallel computation and a time-to-space transformation. Experimental evaluations demonstrate the superiority of Quasi-Periodic WaveNet over state-of-the-art models in audio signal reconstruction, and its versatility is showcased through its application in end-to-end speech synthesis.

This study introduces MADARi, a comprehensive web platform designed for
executing NLP tasks in under-resourced North African dialects, specifically
Algerian Arabic. The platform enables the annotation of various linguistic
features, including morphology, syntax, and coreference, with a focus on
Named Entity Recognition (NER) and Spelling Modification (SEM) in this study.
Madari leverages Almorabit, a unified annotation tool capable of annotating
multiple layers of linguistic markup, facilitating NER and SEM in Algerian
Arabic. The platform has been made accessible to researchers and developers
via the Almorabit Web Interface, and the introduced dataset along with the
MADARi system has been made available to the research community.

This study photochemically modeled temperate terrestrial planets with H2-dominated atmospheres, and analyzed their spectral characteristics using a range of methods. The research focused on the impact of atmospheric composition and temperature on the planets' spectra, and was applied to a range of hypothetical exoplanets, including Kepler-42b, Kepler-78b, and GJ 1214b. The results demonstrated that the planets' spectra are significantly influenced by their atmospheric composition and temperature, and that they exhibit a range of spectral features that could be used to identify and characterize these exoplanets. The research also highlighted the limitations of current detection methods, and the need for further study to accurately determine the physical properties of these exoplanets. The findings were illustrated with a range of spectral plots, and the research has important implications for the future of exoplanet detection and characterization. The research also demonstrated the need for further study to accurately determine the physical properties of these exoplanets, and the limitations of current detection methods. The results of this study have important implications for the future of exoplanet detection and characterization.

To verify the presence of a non-Abelian Majorana zero mode, a unique signature in the zero-bias peak is required. A proposed experiment involves a semiconductor nanowire with an induced superconducting gap, where a voltage is applied across its ends. A distinctive feature of a Majorana zero mode is its self-energies that behave like a step function near zero, in contrast to the linear relationship of ordinary states. This study suggests a more effective method for detecting a Majorana zero mode by utilizing a tunneling spectroscopy setup with resistive barriers and Ohm's law. A key advantage of this method is that it can clearly differentiate a Majorana zero mode from other peaks at zero-bias, based on the distinct self-energy relationship. Furthermore, this study provides analytical and numerical descriptions of the tunneling conductance, showing that a major peak at zero-bias will exhibit a unique self-energy that varies inversely with resistance, as opposed to the linear relationship of ordinary states.

The advent of deep learning in computer vision has led to the creation of automatic systems for detecting road problems, resulting in a variety of methods being developed to identify issues like cracks, potholes, and other hazards. However, there is a lack of consensus on the classification and reporting of these defects, which complicates the standardization of data and hinders the effective use of this information for maintenance and repair planning. To address this issue, we have created RoadAtlas, an open-source platform that leverages deep learning for the automatic detection of defects from videos captured by vehicles, while also providing a unified classification system and a georeferenced data management system. By integrating these features, RoadAtlas not only facilitates the extraction of critical information from video footage but also ensures that this data can be used for more comprehensive analysis and visualization purposes.
This paper introduces a fresh approach to categorifying shadows using the concept of bicategorical slices.

This study presents the challenging conditional random field method for audio source localization in 3D space. We provide a clear and practical implementation of this approach, which can be used as a starting point for exploring alternative methods like deep learning. Our results are demonstrated with real-world data, successfully localizing sound sources in a three-dimensional environment.

This paper introduces a new type of graph neural network called Lorentzian Graph Neural Networks (LGNNs), which are based on a time-enhanced version of the graph. By leveraging the unique properties of a time-oriented graph, LGNNs can effectively process and learn from time-series data associated with graphs. We demonstrate the effectiveness of LGNNs in various tasks, including node classification and graph-level tasks, by achieving state-of-the-art results on benchmark datasets.

The analysis of structural acoustic interactions involves examining a coherent assembly of a solid body and a fluid surrounding it. This study considers a specific scenario where the interaction between the fluid and the solid is significantly influenced due to a narrowing gap between them. The research focuses on determining possible configurations in which a sudden increase in the gap results in the solid becoming trapped between the fluid and a given boundary above. The study also explores conditions under which the solid remains stable under a specific range of fluid viscosity. The analysis relies on the assumption that the solid's weight is negligible and the fluid's velocity adheres to the no-slip condition at the solid's boundary. The study utilizes the decomposition of the Navier-Stokes equations into manageable components for analysis.

In optics, compressing light into small spaces has numerous applications, yet there's a limited equivalent option in mechanics due to difficulties in achieving spatial compression for phonons. This work demonstrates the ability to transfer a phonon into a photon in a static, compressed environment using optomechanical technology. By combining an optical waveguide and a cavity, the experiment takes advantage of their different wavelength scales to reduce the necessary setup size. Using a mechanical resonator with a large frequency range, the experiment is able to achieve efficient compression transfer under difficult conditions. This approach may be useful in future experiments and could be applied in the field of quantum technology.

We examine the fundamental characteristics of the classical scalar and vectorial mu-calculus in contrast to their extended versions that incorporate action modalities. The basic features of a parametric variant of the planetary mu-calculus are also explored.

We present a novel efficient exponential delay discounting model influenced by the Tsallis framework. By leveraging the maximal entropy principle, we derive the probability distribution for patience and demonstrate that our framework can be understood through the lens of thermodynamics. Specifically, mapping the Tsallis framework to thermodynamics reveals that our maximum uncertainty represents maximum entropy, delay discounting follows the Nernst theorem, and the framework's efficiency can be explained using a free energy concept. Additionally, we propose that the Tsallis parameter may be related to impatience. Our theoretical advancements lead to novel, testable predictions.
We discuss the concept of a harmonic gauge within Substantial General Relativity (SGR) and the unique property of defining a harmonic gauge in this theory.

We investigate the notion of extended double covers for signed graphs, which builds upon the concept of extended double covers for ordinary graphs. In contrast to ordinary graphs, not all signed graphs possess homomorphisms to their extended double covers. Specifically, we examine the set of countable tuples of functions that can map to extended double covers and determine their limiting structure. Furthermore, our research provides a characterization of those countable signed graphs whose behavior can be described by first-order logic in relation to their extended double covers. Additionally, we explore the relationship between this characterization and the study of homomorphism densities between large sparse graphs.
The Weyl-Wigner representation has been utilized to translate the canonical equilibrium conditions into a form that can be effectively applied in engineering practice.

The concept of negative absolute temperature has historically been viewed with skepticism in the thermodynamics community, largely due to its initial discovery being limited to specific systems such as spin ensembles that decoupled from their surroundings. These circumstances led many to believe negative temperatures were merely a theoretical oddity with no practical relevance. However, this perspective is undergoing a shift as recent breakthroughs in the field of mesoscale physics enable the creation of thermal environments with negative temperatures. These findings demonstrate that such unusual temperatures can facilitate new types of heat engine designs, some of which can surpass the efficiency limits imposed by traditional heat engines that operate between two positive temperature reservoirs.

Let $A$ and $B$ be non-empty finite subsets of integers. For any integer $c$, we define the following constrained sumsets:  
$\sigma(A,B,c) = \{a+b \mid a\in A, b\in B, a+b=c\}$ and $\tau(A,B,c) = \{a-b \mid a\in A, b\in B, a+b=c\}$.  
Recent research has been done on the maximum cardinality of $\sigma(A,B,c)$ and $\tau(A,B,c)$.  
In this study, we establish two new results:  
First, the maximum cardinality of $\sigma(A,B,c)$ is at most $|A|+|B|-1$, with the equality holding under specific conditions on the sets $A$ and $B$.  
Second, the maximum cardinality of $\tau(A,B,c)$ is at most $|A|+|B|-1$, with the equality holding under different specific scenarios.  
We also prove an exact maximum cardinality of $\tau(A,B,c)$ and obtain a bound of $|A|+|B|-2$ for $\sigma(A,B,c)$.  
Additionally, some constrained difference sets with the same sum are discussed.

The recent advancements in deep learning have significantly improved automated medical diagnosis systems, particularly in identifying and detecting diseases.

However, the high cost of expert annotation has slowed progress in developing these automated diagnosis systems.

A historical dataset, labeled by expert pathologists, is crucial for training and evaluating effective algorithms for accurate disease detection.

In this paper, we provide UniToPatho, a comprehensive histological dataset comprising 14,000 images that can be used for the classification of colorectal polyps and the evaluation of adenoma dysplasia.

UniToPatho is suitable for training algorithms to assist endoscopists in identifying areas of concern during colonoscopy procedures.

We present experimental results utilizing UniToPatho and compare our performance with existing methods, including those on the Kvasir-Polyps-v2 and the recent HiPCo datasets.

Our findings demonstrate that our algorithm achieves a macro F1 score of 0.915 in binary polyp classification and scores of 0.745 and 0.741 in the three-class and two-stage adenoma dysplasia evaluation tasks, respectively.

Additionally, UniToPatho was ranked third in the HiPCo challenge's binary polyp classification track, achieving a macro F1 score of 0.914.

This research addresses wave scattering problems by obstacles with complex shapes, accounting for material absorption. We examine the acoustic wave equation as frequency increases and address the challenges that arise from smoothly changing material properties. A new approach is proposed using the finite element method to efficiently solve the problem. We establish the reliability of our method and demonstrate its effectiveness through the scattering of a plane wave from a sphere, successfully capturing the transition from the shadow region to the lit region.

A two-tiered model of early solar system formation, consisting of dry and moist planetesimals, is supported by new data. Drying events, which led to the formation of moist planetesimals, occurred in the inner solar system approximately 3.3 to 3.5 million years after it began. The discovery of the isotopic composition of water within the CAIs in meteorites Chelyabinsk and Benenitra, which date back 4.567 million years, supports this model. The water found in these meteorites was locked within H2O-rich moist planetesimals that collided with the central body in the inner solar system around 200,000 kilometers from the Sun. The Chelyabinsk and Benenitra meteorites provide the first direct evidence for the existence of moist planetesimals in the inner solar system. The discovery of these meteorites also suggests that the water found on Earth, which started accumulating around 4.56 million years ago, originated from the collision of these moist planetesimals with the early Earth. The formation of dry and moist planetesimals, which were separated by drying events, was a common occurrence in the inner solar system, and the discovery of these two meteorites is not an isolated event.

Using the algebraic method, we derive exact expressions for the large-spectral-density limit of spin-chain form factors for a specific class of local operators. This limit can be numerically computed and the results show a direct correlation with the underlying operator's affine quantum-algebra symmetry. Such symmetry causes the formation of distinct clusters within the continuous spectrum, and the algebraic method takes advantage of these clusters to perform accurate numerical evaluations. We extend our analysis to two different spin-chain models and find that the formed clusters persist, indicating the presence of the same deep symmetries.

This paper introduces a novel approach for voice translation that achieves zero-shot translation. Our method leverages pre-trained language and voice generation models, utilizing their latent language and voice generation series as intermediaries. This allows for the translation of a target language from a source language without the need for additional training. Notably, our approach can also translate between source and target languages with differing numbers of channels. Experimental results demonstrate the system's capability to translate between English and German, Japanese and Korean, and Mandarin Chinese and Vietnamese.

In the context of electromagnetic wave scattering and its subsequent influence, the multipolar expansions of 3D vector fields are extensively utilized. These expansions are highly versatile and extensively applied in various fields, including radar, remote sensing, and acoustic imaging. Nevertheless, existing literature often restricts their application within the dipole approximation, which is limited to scenarios where the wavelength is significantly larger than the object being analyzed. This restriction excludes a substantial number of practical applications. This research introduces an innovative approach to expand time-harmonic electromagnetic waves into a multipolar basis, which not only covers the scattering process but also accurately accounts for the wave's interaction with surfaces, thereby enabling precise calculation of optical properties. This method is demonstrated to be effective in predicting scattering patterns and surface properties, such as absorption and transmission, for 2D objects across a broad spectrum of wavelengths.

This study introduces immanants of young tableaux and establishes the immanant of a direct sum of young tableaux as the product of individual immanants. A new algebra, Quantum Double Young-Capelli, is defined with generators from double Young tableaux and its relationship to quantum Schur algebras and Young algebras is examined. Furthermore, connections between quantum immanants of young tableaux and the quantum 6j-symbols of angular momenta are analyzed. A link between immanants of standard young tableaux and the Casimir operators of Lie algebras is also demonstrated. To achieve this, formulas for the quantum immanants of standard young tableaux are derived using both Littlewood-Richardson rule and Littlewood identity, which in turn enable proof of relations to 6j-symbols and Casimir elements, and to establish that immanants of standard young tableaux are invariant under row permutations.

Within the most elementary scoto-seesaw model, we investigate the connections between see-saw induced neutrino masses and the dark matter abundance, established through extended Standard Model interactions. Analyzing a range of parameter sets, we determine the impact of extended Standard Model interactions on dark matter density and examine the stability of the Standard Model vacuum under various conditions. Furthermore, we identify the limits of validity for the see-saw mechanism and investigate the potential for detecting dark matter in direct experiments.

The concept of $t_{2g}$-$e_g$ orbital hybridization is explored for transition metals in various oxidation states from +1 to +7. Due to increased electronegativity and better spatial overlap with ligands in higher oxidation states, hybridization is more common in these states. Examples of materials with this property are provided for metals in +1, +2, +3, +4, +5, +6, and +7 states, with the majority featuring 3d metals. Nevertheless, examples of 4d and 5d metals in +2, +3, +4, +5, +6, and +7 states are also presented. Although orbital hybridization typically disrupts the formation of distinct $t_{2g}$ or $e_g$ bands, it can be beneficial to retain some degree of symmetry. Consequently, some materials with this characteristic exhibit interesting physical properties, such as magnetoelectric effects and multiferroicity.

We introduce a novel expansion of the space Rqnp(X) for a projective variety X, which incorporates altered varieties of X through birational transformations. The expansion is equipped with a canonical topological structure that forms a directed set, allowing for the integration of additional birational modifications of X. The underlying lattice of this expanded space exhibits comprehensive stability properties, including compactness, completeness, and computability. The subspaces corresponding to the original variety X and its smooth, projective varieties display isomorphic structural properties. The topological framework of this expanded space displays continuity across specific classes of birational transformations that preserve the geometric and topological integrity of X. The properties of this expanded space provide a more in-depth understanding of the relationship between quantum and classical algebraic topologies. The research is supported by the discovery that the fundamental group of X remains invariant across the expanded space and that certain subspaces exhibit rich algebraic structures. The findings have significant implications for the study of quantum and classical algebraic topologies and may lead to novel approaches in this field. The research is further characterized by the exploration of the universal covering and homology properties of X and its expanded space, which reveal the complex interplay between the algebraic and topological structures of these spaces. The research is also marked by the discovery that the cohomology of X exhibits a rich combinatorial structure that reflects the underlying algebraic and topological relationships between X and its expanded space. Our research team has developed a new approach to create a dataset for training deep learning models that can accurately predict the presence of diseases in chest X-rays. To achieve this, we designed an image modification technique that can mark specific regions in radiographs based on the symptoms of common conditions such as pneumonia, tuberculosis, and COVID-19. This innovative method enables us to generate a balanced dataset with a 1:1 ratio of positive to negative samples, which in turn allows us to train effective binary classification models. We have tested our method on publicly available datasets and successfully produced a balanced dataset containing 10,000 annotated images.

This note introduces ViDaExpert, a cutting-edge graphical examination and visualization tool for multidimensional vector data. Utilizing cutting-edge nonlinear dimensionality reduction techniques like t-SNE and UMAP, this tool enables a deep understanding of data structure and feature relationships. ViDaExpert integrates various visualization components and automated feature ranking to facilitate seamless data exploration, providing users with an intuitive and efficient examination process.

This paper provides a detailed examination of Newtonian potential calculation 
on flat domains using several approaches within the framework of $\mathbb{R}^n$. 
Multiple algorithms are presented for differentiating under the integral sign, 
utilizing fast convolution methods, and employing finite element methods. 
A key contribution is the development of a differential framework for 
Newtonian potential calculation on flat domains, allowing for efficient 
computation through differentiation, convolution, and simulation. 
Several examples are provided to illustrate the effectiveness of these 
algorithms in terms of accuracy and computational speed.
